subject: Transient SLA adjustment request — Vision beta onboarding
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Jillian Park <jillian@nebula.health>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient SLA adjustment request — Vision beta onboarding

Hi all,

Nebula Health is starting a narrow beta of their vision module (image-to-text triage) next week and they've asked for a short-term SLO carveout while we stabilize the new model variant (vision-v2-beta). Key asks from the customer: a) relax P95 latency from 350ms to 700ms for the first 72 hours of rollout, and b) a tolerance for a higher error budget for image-heavy requests during canary.

What I'm proposing:
- Approve a time-boxed exception (72 hours) for P95 to 700ms for requests routed to vision-v2-beta.
- Require automatic fallback to a stable CPU-quantized vision-v1 endpoint if latency > 1s or confidence < threshold.
- Enable heightened tracing and prefix-KV cache for the beta traffic; we will ship a short trace bundle to Nebula.
- Canary at 5% traffic for 24h, then 20% for 24h, then ramp to 100% if no regressions.

I attached a compact proposal (vision_beta_slo_proposal.pdf) and a canary checklist (canary-plan-20260921.md).

Requesting quick sign-off so we can include the exception in the onboarding playbook and get Nebula's legal to sign the exception doc. Rafael / Aditya: any operational or compliance blockers? Lauren: can you coordinate the enhanced tracing runbook? Jillian: confirm you can accept the temporary SLO change in writing.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vision_beta_slo_proposal.pdf (PDF, 48KB); canary-plan-20260921.md (text, 6KB)

From: Jillian Park <jillian@nebula.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient SLA adjustment request — Vision beta onboarding

Diego — thanks for the quick note and the proposal. A few clarifying questions before we sign: 

1) Will the exception be limited to Nebula's project id (NB-2387) and isolated from our other workloads?
2) If we hit the 1s fallback threshold, will requests to the fallback model be billed at the standard rate or will there be a different accounting?
3) Can you provide a short list of telemetry we'll receive during the 72h window (traces, per-route p95, error rates)?

We appreciate the canary plan. From our side we need a written confirmation that data routing and retention remain unchanged and that logs are scoped to our org. If you can send the signed exception (DocuSign link) and the telemetry export config, we'll review it today.

—Jillian
Jillian Park
Director, Platform Operations
Nebula Health

[ops@nebula.health]

Subject: Re: Transient SLA adjustment request — Vision beta onboarding

Diego — quick operational notes:
- I can own the tracing runbook and will add the export config to the Drive link (see related_links).
- We should require Nebula's traffic to be routed via a dedicated route key so we can apply prefix caching and per-tenant limits. Rafael, can you confirm the route key and whether Dedicated pooling is required?
- On billing: recommend we bill fallback requests at the standard hosted rate but annotate invoices with a one-time onboarding credit (negotiated with sales). Finance sign-off needed.

I'll review the attached proposal and add inline comments. If we get sign-off by EOD tomorrow, Eng can schedule the canary runbook for Thursday.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Jillian Park <jillian@nebula.health>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient SLA adjustment request — Vision beta onboarding

Thanks Lauren. Uploading the revised proposal with explicit telemetry fields and fallbacks (attached). Highlights:
- Explicit SLO window: 2026-09-24T08:00:00Z to 2026-09-27T08:00:00Z (72 hours).
- P95 adjusted to 700ms only for requests tagged with route_key=nebula-nb2387-beta.
- Auto-fallback policy: if 5-min moving average latency > 1000ms OR model confidence CI < 0.82, route to vision-v1-stable and mark event in trace.
- Billing note: fallback calls billed at standard per-token/per-embedding rates; sales will issue a one-time onboarding credit equal to 20% of the predicted token spend for the 72h window.

Attached: vision_beta_slo_proposal.pdf, latency-traces_0921.zip (sample traces).

Jillian — telemetry export will include: per-route p50/p95/p99, error_rate, sample traces (5% of requests), and a per-request model confidence score. We'll redact any PHI fields before export.

Can we get a short written reply from Nebula confirming acceptance? Rafael / Aditya: if there are no other blockers, can we proceed to issue the DocuSign exception and lock the canary schedule?

Diego
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vision_beta_slo_proposal.pdf (updated, 72KB); latency-traces_0921.zip (sample traces, 6MB)

Diego — forwarding with conditional approval.

We will allow the 72-hour P95 increase to 700ms under the following conditions:
1) DocuSign exception is executed by Nebula (link in related_links).
2) Compliance signs off on the telemetry export configuration (no PHI persisted; export is aggregated/sample-only).
3) Engineering implements automatic fallback and an automated rollback if error_rate increases > 3% absolute or latency remains >1s for >15m.
4) We capture the canary runbook in the customer playbook and mark this as a time-limited carveout that will not be precedent-setting without executive review.

Lauren: please loop in Compliance and Eng on the telemetry artifact. Rafael: prepare the billing annotation and onboarding credit. Diego: when the DocuSign is signed, send the signed copy to legal@redwood.ai and cc compliance@redwood.ai.
